Given it is President Trump who reduced U.S. forces in Romania, it’s likely his words that Russia will be watching for.


U.S. Ambassador to NATO (@USAmbNATO)

We stand with our NATO Ally Romania and condemn this reckless incursion on its territory.  Our thoughts are with the injured in Galati.  We will defend every inch of NATO territory.

Russia’s former president the day after a Russian drone strikes NATO ally Romania:


Dmitry Medvedev (@MedvedevRussiaE)

Citizens of EU countries, You should realize your authorities have unilaterally entered into a war with Russia. So be vigilant and don't be surprised by anything. The peaceful sleep is over. But you know who to ask why!



— https://nitter.net/MedvedevRussiaE/status/2060336415498469554#m

European leaders had been warning of a potential Russian attack on NATO:

Overnight, an explosive-laden Russian drone hit an apartment building in Romania early Friday, its government said, as Moscow’s forces attacked a nearby Ukrainian port.

Two people were wounded in the strike, which drew condemnation from fellow NATO member states, while Bucharest urged allies to help with its anti-drone defenses.

Estonian FM @Tsahkna: “I'm very confident that NATO is working.”

What national security interest does it serve to threaten one the U.S.’s oldest allies in the region and one with a military access agreement essential to operations against Iran?


Aaron Rupar (@atrupar)

Meet the @TheStudyofWar researchers who say the Ukraine war has entered a new phase to Ukraine’s advantage and that now is the time for its allies to provide crucial help.

Video

Fact is, Eastern European leaders have been warning for years they are Russia’s next targets. EU FM @kajakallas told me in “The Return of Great Powers” in 2024:

“So far, nobody thought Russia would test NATO’s unity, but we have seen that they have acted in conflict with all the laws that we might have. So, we have to be prepared. As Russia has boosted the level of aggression, we have to boost the level of defense.”


The Wall Street Journal (@WSJ)

Russia is stuck on the Ukrainian battlefield

Question: As Ukraine shares advanced drone technology with the U.S., is it safe to say Ukraine does have cards now in this conflict?

Ukrainian Amb @StefanishynaO: “We printed them. We might have shortages and access to good cards, but we had to invent them. Yes, we made our own.”

Video

Today, Ukrainian Amb to the U.S.  @StefanishynaO tells me that Russia is counting on “further shortages of air defense ammunition because of the war in Iran”, which helped spark “one of the most brutal” missile barrages since Russia’s full-scale invasion,

Video

Breaking: The US military says it conducted “self-defense strikes” targeting Iranian missile launch sites and boats around the Strait of Hormuz on Monday amid a ceasefire between the two countries and ongoing negotiations to end the war, according to US Central Command.

“U.S. forces conducted self-defense strikes in southern Iran today to protect our troops from threats posed by Iranian forces,” CENTCOM spokesman Timothy Hawkins told CNN in a statement when asked about explosions reported aroun

Breaking. Three explosions were heard in the port city of Bandar Abbas, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said in a short statement on Monday citing “sources,” but there was no immediate official confirmation of the cause of the blasts. “Further updates will be announced subsequently,” the IRGC added in the statement. -@CNN

Overnight: Russia used a new hypersonic ballistic missile in one of its biggest bombardments of the Kyiv region since the war began, an attack that left at least four people dead. Its speed and trajectory make italmost unstoppable by the air defense systems available to Ukraine. It is only the third time Russia has used the missile. -@CNN

I’ve been asking European officials and diplomats for their reaction to U.S. force reductions and other attacks on the alliance for months and not one has told me this is “business as usual.”


Teri Schultz (@terischultz)

#NATO chief Rutte calls the expected US reduction in its contributions to the NATO Force Model (alliance's response to crises), to be discussed among deputy political directors Friday at NATO HQ, have been underway for a year. He calls them "structured" and "business as usual.
